sanskrit: yac cāpi dravyam upayujyate ha; vānaspatyam āyasaṃ pārthivaṃ vā divyena rūpeṇa ca prajñayā ca; tenaiva siddhir iti viddhi vidvan
english: Know this, O learned one: whatever material is used — whether of plant, metal, or earth — it is through divine form and wisdom together that perfection is achieved.

sanskrit: tārkṣya uvāca idaṃ śreyaḥ paramaṃ manyamānā; vyāyacchante munayaḥ saṃpratītāḥ ācakṣva me taṃ paramaṃ viśokaṃ; mokṣaṃ paraṃ yaṃ praviśanti dhīrāḥ
english: Tārkṣya said: The sages of established repute, considering this the supreme good, strive for it. Tell me of that supreme liberation, free from sorrow, into which the wise enter.

sanskrit: sarasvaty uvāca taṃ vai paraṃ vedavidaḥ prapannāḥ; paraṃ parebhyaḥ prathitaṃ purāṇam svādhyāyadānavratapuṇyayogais; tapodhanā vītaśokā vimuktāḥ
english: Sarasvatī said: Those who know the Vedas have attained to that supreme state — the ancient one proclaimed as highest among the high. Ascetics enriched by self-study, charity, vows, and meritorious practice are freed from sorrow and liberated.

sanskrit: tasyātha madhye vetasaḥ puṇyagandhaḥ; sahasraśākho vimalo vibhāti tasya mūlāt saritaḥ prasravanti; madhūdakaprasravaṇā ramaṇyaḥ
english: In the midst of that realm there shines a holy-scented reed with a thousand branches, pure and resplendent; from its roots flow rivers, delightful streams flowing with honey-sweet waters.

sanskrit: śākhāṃ śākhāṃ mahānadyaḥ saṃyānti sikatāsamāḥ dhānāpūpā māṃsaśākāḥ sadā pāyasakardamāḥ
english: Toward branch after branch great rivers flow, their sands fine as grain; there are parched grain and cakes, meat and vegetables, and always currents of milk-pudding flowing like streams of mud.

sanskrit: yasminn agnimukhā devāḥ sendrāḥ saha marudgaṇaiḥ ījire kratubhiḥ śreṣṭhais tat padaṃ paramaṃ mune
english: In that place, O sage, the gods led by Indra, having fire as their mouth, together with the Marut hosts have worshipped with the most excellent sacrificial rites — that is the supreme abode.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ sa pāṇḍavo bhūyo mārkaṇḍeyam uvāca ha kathayasveha caritaṃ manor vaivasvatasya me
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the son of Pāṇḍu spoke again to Mārkaṇḍeya: "Tell me here the deeds of Manu, the son of Vivasvat."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca vivasvataḥ suto rājan paramarṣiḥ pratāpavān babhūva naraśārdūla prajāpatisamadyutiḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: The son of Vivasvat, O king, became a great sage, mighty in glory, O tiger among men, with a radiance equal to that of Prajāpati.

sanskrit: ojasā tejasā lakṣmyā tapasā ca viśeṣataḥ aticakrāma pitaraṃ manuḥ svaṃ ca pitāmaham
english: In vigor, brilliance, prosperity, and especially in austerity, Manu surpassed his own father and his grandfather as well.

sanskrit: ūrdhvabāhur viśālāyāṃ badaryāṃ sa narādhipaḥ ekapādasthitas tīvraṃ cacāra sumahat tapaḥ
english: That lord of men, standing on one foot with arms raised in the great expanse of Badarī forest, performed fierce and exceedingly great austerity.

sanskrit: avākśirās tathā cāpi netrair animiṣair dṛḍham so 'tapyata tapo ghoraṃ varṣāṇām ayutaṃ tadā
english: With head bent down and eyes unwinking, firm and steadfast, he then practiced terrible austerity for ten thousand years.

sanskrit: taṃ kadā cit tapasyantam ārdracīrajaṭādharam vīriṇītīram āgamya matsyo vacanam abravīt
english: Once, while he was practicing austerity, wearing wet bark garments and matted locks, a fish came to the bank of the Vīriṇī river and spoke to him.

sanskrit: bhagavan kṣudramatsyo 'smi balavadbhyo bhayaṃ mama matsyebhyo hi tato māṃ tvaṃ trātum arhasi suvrata
english: "Blessed one, I am a small fish; I am afraid of the stronger ones, for fishes eat fishes — therefore you, O one of holy vows, should protect me."

sanskrit: durbalaṃ balavanto hi matsyaṃ matsyā viśeṣataḥ bhakṣayanti yathā vṛttir vihitā naḥ sanātanī
english: "Indeed, the strong ones especially devour the weak fish — such is the eternal law of conduct ordained for us."

sanskrit: tasmād bhayaughān mahato majjantaṃ māṃ viśeṣataḥ trātum arhasi kartāsmi kṛte pratikṛtaṃ tava
english: "Therefore, as I sink especially beneath this great flood of fear, you should protect me; in return I will render back what you have done for me."

sanskrit: sa matsyavacanaṃ śrutvā kṛpayābhipariplutaḥ manur vaivasvato 'gṛhṇāt taṃ matsyaṃ pāṇinā svayam
english: Hearing the fish's words, overwhelmed with compassion, Manu Vaivasvata himself took that fish in his own hands.

sanskrit: udakāntam upānīya matsyaṃ vaivasvato manuḥ aliñjare prākṣipat sa candrāṃśusadṛśaprabham
english: Manu Vaivasvata, having brought it to the water's edge, placed that fish — radiant as the rays of the moon — into a jar.

sanskrit: sa tatra vavṛdhe rājan matsyaḥ paramasatkṛtaḥ putravac cākarot tasmin manur bhāvaṃ viśeṣataḥ
english: There the fish grew, O king, treated with the utmost care, and Manu developed a particularly fond feeling toward it, as toward a son.

sanskrit: atha kālena mahatā sa matsyaḥ sumahān abhūt aliñjare jale caiva nāsau samabhavat kila
english: Then, after a long time, that fish grew exceedingly large, and it no longer fit at all in the water of the jar.

sanskrit: atha matsyo manuṃ dṛṣṭvā punar evābhyabhāṣata bhagavan sādhu me 'dyānyat sthānaṃ saṃpratipādaya
english: Then, seeing Manu, the fish spoke to him again: "Blessed one, please provide me another suitable place today."

sanskrit: uddhṛtyāliñjarāt tasmāt tataḥ sa bhagavān muniḥ taṃ matsyam anayad vāpīṃ mahatīṃ sa manus tadā
english: Then that blessed sage Manu, having lifted the fish from the jar, brought it to a great pond.

sanskrit: tatra taṃ prākṣipac cāpi manuḥ parapuraṃjaya athāvardhata matsyaḥ sa punar varṣagaṇān bahūn
english: Manu placed it there, O conqueror of enemy cities, and the fish grew again for many more years.

sanskrit: dviyojanāyatā vāpī vistṛtā cāpi yojanam tasyāṃ nāsau samabhavan matsyo rājīvalocana viceṣṭituṃ vā kaunteya matsyo vāpyāṃ viśāṃ pate
english: The pond was two yojanas long and one yojana wide; the fish, O lotus-eyed one, could no longer fit in it, O son of Kuntī, O lord of peoples — nor could it move freely in the pond.

sanskrit: manuṃ matsyas tato dṛṣṭvā punar evābhyabhāṣata naya māṃ bhagavan sādho samudramahiṣīṃ prabho gaṅgāṃ tatra nivatsyāmi yathā vā tāta manyase
english: Then seeing Manu, the fish spoke to him again: "Lead me, blessed and noble lord, to the Gaṅgā, queen of the ocean — I will dwell there, or as you think best, dear one."

sanskrit: evam ukto manur matsyam anayad bhagavān vaśī nadīṃ gaṅgāṃ tatra cainaṃ svayaṃ prākṣipad acyutaḥ
english: Thus addressed, Manu the self-controlled blessed one brought the fish to the river Gaṅgā and himself placed it there.

sanskrit: sa tatra vavṛdhe matsyaḥ kiṃ cit kālam ariṃdama tataḥ punar manuṃ dṛṣṭvā matsyo vacanam abravīt
english: The fish grew there for some time, O subduer of foes; then seeing Manu again, the fish spoke these words.

sanskrit: gaṅgāyāṃ hi na śaknomi bṛhattvāc ceṣṭituṃ prabho samudraṃ naya mām āśu prasīda bhagavann iti
english: "In the Gaṅgā I am no longer able to move freely, being so large, O lord; take me quickly to the ocean — be gracious, O blessed one."

sanskrit: uddhṛtya gaṅgāsalilāt tato matsyaṃ manuḥ svayam samudram anayat pārtha tatra cainam avāsṛjat
english: Lifting the fish from the waters of the Gaṅgā, Manu himself then brought it, O Pārtha, to the ocean and released it there.

sanskrit: sumahān api matsyaḥ san sa manor manasas tadā āsīd yatheṣṭahāryaś ca sparśagandhasukhaś ca vai
english: Though grown exceedingly large, the fish was then as if drawn by Manu's very mind — delightful to behold, pleasing to touch and smell.

sanskrit: yadā samudre prakṣiptaḥ sa matsyo manunā tadā tata enam idaṃ vākyaṃ smayamāna ivābravīt
english: When that fish had been cast into the ocean by Manu, it then spoke these words to him, smiling as it were.

sanskrit: bhagavan kṛtā hi me rakṣā tvayā sarvā viśeṣataḥ prāptakālaṃ tu yat kāryaṃ tvayā tac chrūyatāṃ mama
english: "Blessed one, you have given me complete and exceptional protection; now hear from me what you must do when the time arrives."

sanskrit: acirād bhagavan bhaumam idaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam sarvam eva mahābhāga pralayaṃ vai gamiṣyati
english: "Before long, O blessed and great one, all of this earth — both the moving and the unmoving — will surely go to dissolution."

sanskrit: saṃprakṣālanakālo 'yaṃ lokānāṃ samupasthitaḥ tasmāt tvāṃ bodhayāmy adya yat te hitam anuttamam
english: "The time for the washing away of the worlds has arrived; therefore I alert you today to what is of supreme benefit to you."

sanskrit: trasānāṃ sthāvarāṇāṃ ca yac ceṅgaṃ yac ca neṅgati tasya sarvasya saṃprāptaḥ kālaḥ paramadāruṇaḥ
english: "The dreadful time has arrived for all of it — for animals and plants alike, for whatever moves and whatever does not move."

sanskrit: nauś ca kārayitavyā te dṛḍhā yuktavaṭākarā tatra saptarṣibhiḥ sārdham āruhethā mahāmune
english: "You must have a strong ship built, equipped with ropes of hemp; together with the seven sages you shall board it, O great sage."

sanskrit: bījāni caiva sarvāṇi yathoktāni mayā purā tasyām ārohayer nāvi susaṃguptāni bhāgaśaḥ
english: "And you shall board that ship with all the seeds as previously described by me, well preserved in their different categories."

sanskrit: nausthaś ca māṃ pratīkṣethās tadā munijanapriya āgamiṣyāmy ahaṃ śṛṅgī vijñeyas tena tāpasa
english: "Standing on the ship, you shall then await me, O dear one to the community of sages; I will come bearing a horn — by that you shall know me, O ascetic."

sanskrit: evam etat tvayā kāryam āpṛṣṭo 'si vrajāmy aham nātiśaṅkyam idaṃ cāpi vacanaṃ te mamābhibho
english: "This is what you must do; you have been instructed, I go now; and this word of mine should not be doubted overmuch by you, O mighty one."

sanskrit: evaṃ kariṣya iti taṃ sa matsyaṃ pratyabhāṣata jagmatuś ca yathākāmam anujñāpya parasparam
english: He replied to the fish: "So shall I do"; and having taken leave of each other as they wished, the two parted.

sanskrit: tato manur mahārāja yathoktaṃ matsyakena ha bījāny ādāya sarvāṇi sāgaraṃ pupluve tadā nāvā tu śubhayā vīra mahormiṇam ariṃdama
english: Then Manu, O great king, just as the fish had instructed, took all the seeds and sailed out on the ocean, O hero, on an auspicious ship upon the vast waves, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: cintayām āsa ca manus taṃ matsyaṃ pṛthivīpate sa ca tac cintitaṃ jñātvā matsyaḥ parapuraṃjaya śṛṅgī tatrājagāmāśu tadā bharatasattama
english: And Manu meditated upon that fish, O lord of the earth; knowing that thought, the fish — bearing its horn — swiftly came there then, O best of the Bharatas, O conqueror of enemy cities.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā manujendrendra manur matsyaṃ jalārṇave śṛṅgiṇaṃ taṃ yathoktena rūpeṇādrim ivocchritam
english: Seeing it, O lord among lords of men, Manu beheld the fish in the ocean — horned and risen like a mountain, exactly in the form foretold.

sanskrit: vaṭākaramayaṃ pāśam atha matsyasya mūrdhani manur manujaśārdūla tasmiñ śṛṅge nyaveśayat
english: Then Manu, O tiger among men, placed a noose made of hemp rope on the head of the fish — on that very horn.

sanskrit: saṃyatas tena pāśena matsyaḥ parapuraṃjaya vegena mahatā nāvaṃ prākarṣal lavaṇāmbhasi
english: Bound by that noose, the fish, O conqueror of enemy cities, drew the ship with great speed across the salt sea.

sanskrit: sa tatāra tayā nāvā samudraṃ manujeśvara nṛtyamānam ivormībhir garjamānam ivāmbhasā
english: He crossed the ocean in that ship, O lord of men, the sea as if dancing with its waves and roaring with its waters.

sanskrit: kṣobhyamāṇā mahāvātaiḥ sā naus tasmin mahodadhau ghūrṇate capaleva strī mattā parapuraṃjaya
english: Tossed by mighty winds, the ship whirled about on that great ocean like a fickle, intoxicated woman, O conqueror of enemy cities.

sanskrit: naiva bhūmir na ca diśaḥ pradiśo vā cakāśire sarvam āmbhasam evāsīt khaṃ dyauś ca narapuṃgava
english: Neither earth nor the directions nor the intermediate directions were visible; all was nothing but water — and sky and heaven, O bull among men.

sanskrit: evaṃbhūte tadā loke saṃkule bharatarṣabha adṛśyanta saptarṣayo manur matsyaḥ sahaiva ha
english: With the world in such a condition and in confusion, O bull of the Bharatas, the seven sages, Manu, and the fish alone were visible.

sanskrit: evaṃ bahūn varṣagaṇāṃs tāṃ nāvaṃ so 'tha matsyakaḥ cakarṣātandrito rājaṃs tasmin salilasaṃcaye
english: Thus for many years the fish tirelessly pulled that ship, O king, across that expanse of water.

sanskrit: tato himavataḥ śṛṅgaṃ yat paraṃ puruṣarṣabha tatrākarṣat tato nāvaṃ sa matsyaḥ kurunandana
english: Then the fish pulled the ship to the highest peak of the Himālayas, O bull among men, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīt tadā matsyas tān ṛṣīn prahasañ śanaiḥ asmin himavataḥ śṛṅge nāvaṃ badhnīta māciram
english: Then the fish gently said with a laugh to those sages: "Bind the ship quickly to this peak of the Himālayas."

sanskrit: sā baddhā tatra tais tūrṇam ṛṣibhir bharatarṣabha naur matsyasya vacaḥ śrutvā śṛṅge himavatas tadā
english: It was quickly bound there by those sages, O bull of the Bharatas, the ship — hearing the words of the fish — to the peak of the Himālayas then.

sanskrit: tac ca naubandhanaṃ nāma śṛṅgaṃ himavataḥ param khyātam adyāpi kaunteya tad viddhi bharatarṣabha
english: And that highest peak of the Himālayas, known as Naubandhanam — the Ship's Mooring — is famous even today; know this, O son of Kuntī, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: athābravīd animiṣas tān ṛṣīn sahitāṃs tadā ahaṃ prajāpatir brahmā matparaṃ nādhigamyate matsyarūpeṇa yūyaṃ ca mayāsmān mokṣitā bhayāt
english: Then the unblinking one spoke to those assembled sages: "I am Prajāpati Brahmā; nothing higher than me is attainable. In fish form, by me, you have been saved from this danger."

sanskrit: manunā ca prajāḥ sarvāḥ sadevāsuramānavāḥ sraṣṭavyāḥ sarvalokāś ca yac ceṅgaṃ yac ca neṅgati
english: "And by Manu all beings must be created — gods, asuras, and humans — and all the worlds, both the moving and the unmoving."

sanskrit: tapasā cātitīvreṇa pratibhāsya bhaviṣyati matprasādāt prajāsarge na ca mohaṃ gamiṣyati
english: "Through the most intense austerity he will shine forth, and by my grace in the work of creation he will not fall into delusion."

sanskrit: ity uktvā vacanaṃ matsyaḥ kṣaṇenādarśanaṃ gataḥ sraṣṭukāmaḥ prajāś cāpi manur vaivasvataḥ svayam pramūḍho 'bhūt prajāsarge tapas tepe mahat tataḥ
english: Having spoken these words, the fish vanished in a moment. Manu Vaivasvata himself, wishing to create beings, became bewildered at the act of creation and thereafter practiced great austerity.

sanskrit: tapasā mahatā yuktaḥ so 'tha sraṣṭuṃ pracakrame sarvāḥ prajā manuḥ sākṣād yathāvad bharatarṣabha
english: Armed with great austerity, Manu then proceeded to create all beings directly and properly, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: ity etan mātsyakaṃ nāma purāṇaṃ parikīrtitam ākhyānam idam ākhyātaṃ sarvapāpaharaṃ mayā
english: This is the ancient Mātsyaka legend, thus celebrated; this narrative has been recited by me — it removes all sins.

sanskrit: ya idaṃ śṛṇuyān nityaṃ manoś caritam āditaḥ sa sukhī sarvasiddhārthaḥ svargalokam iyān naraḥ
english: The man who regularly hears from the beginning this account of Manu's deeds shall be happy, successful in all purposes, and shall attain the heavenly world.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ sa punar evātha mārkaṇḍeyaṃ yaśasvinam papraccha vinayopeto dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the dharma-king Yudhiṣṭhira, endowed with humility, questioned the illustrious Mārkaṇḍeya again.

sanskrit: naike yugasahasrāntās tvayā dṛṣṭā mahāmune na cāpīha samaḥ kaś cid āyuṣā tava vidyate varjayitvā mahātmānaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ parameṣṭhinam
english: "O great sage, you have witnessed the ends of many thousands of yugas, and no one here is equal to your lifespan, save only the great-souled brahmin Parameṣṭhin."

sanskrit: anantarikṣe loke 'smin devadānavavarjite tvam eva pralaye vipra brahmāṇam upatiṣṭhasi
english: "In this world devoid of sky, bereft of gods and demons, you alone, O brahmin, attend upon Brahmā at the time of dissolution."

sanskrit: pralaye cāpi nirvṛtte prabuddhe ca pitāmahe tvam eva sṛjyamānāni bhūtānīha prapaśyasi
english: "And when dissolution has ended and the Grandfather has awakened, you alone witness the beings being created here."

sanskrit: caturvidhāni viprarṣe yathāvat parameṣṭhinā vāyubhūtā diśaḥ kṛtvā vikṣipyāpas tatas tataḥ
english: "O brahmin sage, the four kinds of beings are created properly by Parameṣṭhin, who, having become wind, sets the directions and scatters the waters this way and that."

sanskrit: tvayā lokaguruḥ sākṣāt sarvalokapitāmahaḥ ārādhito dvijaśreṣṭha tatpareṇa samādhinā
english: "By you, O best of the twice-born, the world's teacher, the Grandfather of all the worlds directly, has been worshipped with meditation wholly fixed on him."

sanskrit: tasmāt sarvāntako mṛtyur jarā vā dehanāśinī na tvā viśati viprarṣe prasādāt parameṣṭhinaḥ
english: "Therefore, O brahmin sage, all-ending death, or old age the destroyer of the body, does not enter into you, by the grace of Parameṣṭhin."

sanskrit: yadā naiva ravir nāgnir na vāyur na ca candramāḥ naivāntarikṣaṃ naivorvī śeṣaṃ bhavati kiṃ cana
english: "When there is neither sun nor fire, neither wind nor moon, neither sky nor earth — when nothing whatsoever remains —"

sanskrit: tasminn ekārṇave loke naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame naṣṭe devāsuragaṇe samutsannamahorage
english: "— in that world become a single ocean, when the moving and the unmoving are destroyed, when the hosts of gods and demons are destroyed, when the great serpents are annihilated —"

sanskrit: śayānam amitātmānaṃ padme padmaniketanam tvam ekaḥ sarvabhūteśaṃ brahmāṇam upatiṣṭhasi
english: "— you alone attend upon the infinite-souled Brahmā lying on a lotus, dwelling in the lotus, the lord of all beings."

sanskrit: etat pratyakṣataḥ sarvaṃ pūrvavṛttaṃ dvijottama tasmād icchāmahe śrotuṃ sarvahetvātmikāṃ kathām
english: "All of this past occurrence was directly witnessed by you, O best of the twice-born. Therefore we wish to hear the narrative that comprehends all causes."

sanskrit: anubhūtaṃ hi bahuśas tvayaikena dvijottama na te 'sty aviditaṃ kiṃ cit sarvalokeṣu nityadā
english: "It has been experienced many times by you alone, O best of the twice-born; there is nothing unknown to you in all the worlds, ever."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca hanta te kathayiṣyāmi namaskṛtvā svayambhuve puruṣāya purāṇāya śāśvatāyāvyayāya ca
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: "Very well, I will tell you — having bowed to the Self-Born, to the Ancient Puruṣa, the Eternal, the Imperishable."

sanskrit: ya eṣa pṛthudīrghākṣaḥ pītavāsā janārdanaḥ eṣa kartā vikartā ca sarvabhāvanabhūtakṛt
english: "He who is this one with broad and long eyes, clothed in yellow — Janārdana — he is the maker and the unmake, the creator of all beings and existences."

sanskrit: acintyaṃ mahad āścaryaṃ pavitram api cottamam anādinidhanaṃ bhūtaṃ viśvam akṣayam avyayam
english: "He is unthinkable, greatly wondrous, supremely pure, without beginning or end, the universal Being, inexhaustible, imperishable."

sanskrit: eṣa kartā na kriyate kāraṇaṃ cāpi pauruṣe yo hy enaṃ puruṣaṃ vetti devā api na taṃ viduḥ
english: "He is the doer but is not done; he is the cause in human affairs. Whoever truly knows this Puruṣa — even the gods do not know him."

sanskrit: sarvam āścaryam evaitan nirvṛttaṃ rājasattama ādito manujavyāghra kṛtsnasya jagataḥ kṣaye
english: "All of this is wondrous indeed, O best of kings, O tiger among men, from the very beginning, at the dissolution of the entire world."

sanskrit: catvāry āhuḥ sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ tat kṛtaṃ yugam tasya tāvac chatī saṃdhyā saṃdhyāṃśaś ca tataḥ param
english: "Four thousand years, they say, is the Kṛta yuga; its twilight is as many hundreds, and after that comes the twilight-portion equally."

sanskrit: trīṇi varṣasahasrāṇi tretāyugam ihocyate tasya tāvac chatī saṃdhyā saṃdhyāṃśaś ca tataḥ param
english: "Three thousand years is here called the Tretā yuga; its twilight is as many hundreds, and after that comes the twilight-portion equally."

sanskrit: tathā varṣasahasre dve dvāparaṃ parimāṇataḥ tasyāpi dviśatī saṃdhyā saṃdhyāṃśaś ca tataḥ param
english: "Likewise two thousand years is the measure of the Dvāpara; its twilight too is two hundred years, and after that the twilight-portion equally."
